title: Cryptography and TLS Insecure Configuration
platform_conditions: Go 1.x standard library (crypto/tls, crypto/subtle, math/rand); applies to all build targets
security_mechanism: Setting tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true} disables the entire certificate chain and hostname verification, turning every TLS connection into an active-MITM target; the vet linter flags it precisely because no compensating check exists in the struct. Tokens and keys drawn from math/rand are predictable: the generator is deterministic from a small seed and its outputs leak state. Comparing MACs or signatures with == leaks a timing oracle that crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare exists to prevent; reusing an AEAD nonce (GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305) with the same key collapses the cipher's security, allowing message forgery after two ciphertexts share a nonce.

source_sink_clues.source: TLS configurations in client/server code, security values produced by math/rand, authenticator comparisons in handlers, and nonce generation for AEAD encryption.
source_sink_clues.sink: tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true}; math/rand/rand for keys, tokens, or nonces; == / bytes.Equal on MACs or signature digests; AES-GCM/ChaCha20 Seal calls reusing a nonce

tracking_guards: Require InsecureSkipVerify be absent (or documented and compensated with a pinned fingerprint verification in VerifyPeerCertificate); require crypto/rand for security values; require subtle.ConstantTimeCompare/hmac.Equal for authenticator comparison; require nonces from a counter or crypto/rand with per-key uniqueness.
not_candidate_when: The skip-verify flag appears only in an explicitly labeled test fixture never executed against production peers, math/rand feeds only non-security sampling, comparison uses subtle/hmac primitives, or nonces are random per message from crypto/rand with negligible collision risk documented for the message volume.
public_references: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/338.html
